thread:
Ana M.: Hey @Jordan / @Sarah — we need a small rerun of the benchmark dataset for the webinar deck. Can you confirm the exact methodology we should cite and a recommended sample payload set?
Mike L.: Also need quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) and warmup strategy documented. webinar is Friday, so tight on time. :alarm_clock:
Jordan R.: Ok — we can run a short sweep. Quick Q: which metrics are must-have for marketing slides? p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and median cost-per-token?
Ana M.: Priorities: p50, p95, p99, tail error rate (% time we hit fallback), and a sample latency distribution heatmap + callout for warm vs cold starts. Call out quantized throughput gains if available.
Sarah T.: We'll need exact input shapes. Marketing provided 3 personas: short-chat (~20 tokens), medium-assist (~120 tokens), long-document (~1024 tokens). Can you give exact JSON payloads?
Mike L.: Example payloads would be great. Also we need a minimal runbook snippet we can paste into slides: what we ran, how many samples, warmup policy, and random seed.
Jordan R.: Working draft of commands below. We'll run 500 samples per cohort, 50 warmup requests per worker. Using the hosted model variant + q8 and q4 for comparison. Run command (example):
```
# run locally against perf infra
curl -X POST https://perf-api.redwood.test/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer PERF-TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1","input":"<payload.json>","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```
Sarah T.: For reporting, Jordan — please return CSV with columns: cohort, model_variant, quant, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, sample_count, warmup_count, seed. Marketing will convert to charts.
perf-bot: run queued: bench-2312345678-q-sweep (submitted by Jordan R.). ETA ~2h.
Ana M.: Can we include a short note about measurement noise and variance decomposition? e.g., 95% CI by bootstrap and per-shard variance. We want to avoid overclaiming.
Jordan R.: Yes — will include methodology blurb: bootstrap CI (1000 resamples), remove cold starts from main percentiles (but include a separate cold-start table), and report mean/std across shards.
Mike L.: One last ask — sample outputs for quality check (5 examples per cohort) so we can sanity-check quantized model quality before we publish.
Sarah T.: We'll flag any >2% semantic regression vs baseline and stop. If that happens we notify marketing immediately.
Jordan R.: Great. I'll post the run artifacts (CSV + samples + short MD runbook) in #marketing as soon as perf-bot finishes. Targeting artifacts up in ~2.5h.
Ana M.: Perfect — thanks. If results look good we'll use q8 numbers in slides and note q4 as experimental. Please ping when ready. :thumbsup:
Mike L.: adding request: include a single-line command we can use in CI to reproduce the headline numbers.
Jordan R.: Will include a reproducible script and the random seed. Last msg before run: confirming cohorts = [short, medium, long], samples=500 each, warmup=50 per worker, quant variants=[fp16,q8,q4], metrics=p50/p95/p99/tokens_per_sec/cost_estimate.
Sarah T.: Ack. Perf-bot will post updates.
perf-bot: bench-2312345678-q-sweep started at 2312345720, job id b-8871.
Ana M.: thanks — standing by for the CSV + samples.
Jordan R.: Uploaded: https://files.redwood/test/bench-2312345678-results.zip (CSV + samples + runbook.md). Quick sanity: median p95 delta q8 vs fp16 = -18% on medium cohort, q4 shows higher variance. Will add CI in the runbook.
Ana M.: Received and downloading now. If we need any tweaks I'll ask here.
